facts.text: The 1888 San Carlos depot, a Richardsonian Romanesque building made of Almaden sandstone, earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places in 1984.
In 1864, Nathaniel Brittan granted railroad right‑of‑way through his land, insisting a station agent and telegraph office stay open at all times.
The city launched the SCOOT shuttle in 2002 to ease hill‑top commutes and replace missing school buses for local residents.
Litton Engineering Laboratories, founded in San Carlos, revolutionized vacuum tube production with the invention of the glass‑blowing lathe.
The San Carlos History Museum displays artifacts from the Ohlone Indians to the space age, tracing the town’s full story.
After establishing a fire station in 1923, San Carlos officially incorporated on July 8, 1925, marking its formal city status.
